sonnet.problem: The card says David tells 'those men' there is something they need to know about the LORD. Psalm 4:3 ('Know that the LORD has set apart the godly...') doesn't say who is being spoken to. The card carries the 'O men' of verse 2 into verse 3 as fact.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

sonnet.problem: The question says David 'wants those men to know' what the LORD has done. The text doesn't say verse 3 is addressed to the men of verse 2, so this presents an open addressee as fact.

sonnet.problem: The card says the first of David's commands is about anger. 'Know that the LORD has set apart the godly...' in verse 3 is already a command that comes before 'Be angry,' and card 7 asked about it. Card 10 repeats the 'first command' claim.
sonnet.rule: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
